lane: Claude 2.1.311 adaptation — invocation grammar re-verification against the 2.1.308 record

help.note: Captured in a disposable environment (COLUMNS unset). Against 2.1.308 only the purge description changed ("Delete a project's Claude Code data (transcripts, tasks, file history, and its entry in ~/.claude.json) from this computer only"); every option and subcommand name and arity is unchanged. The 2.1.308 linux-x64 help is byte-identical to the 2.1.308 darwin-arm64 record.

parseProbes.method: `claude <flags under test> mcp --help`, session-free. Usage "claude mcp" = the flags parse and leave mcp the first operand; the root usage = a flag took mcp as its value, or an unknown option sent the rest to commander's unknown list; exit 1 = commander's own error. Version and help forms exit while parsing.
parseProbes.harness: packages/surface/vendors/claude/census/invocation-probes.mjs, one disposable environment per probe; also run on the 2.1.308 linux-x64 artifact (sha256 356733f185fa988e6bf3aa9a555269fdd167982a2e2a80d3c8a78037bb92ad58, the promoted bytes) for comparison

static.method: Read-only inspection of the digest-pinned executable. Each fact is bound to its anchor by digest and byte offset, and to an 8 KiB window around it by digest; no source text is retained. For 2.1.311 every 2.1.308 anchor was recovered from the promoted darwin-arm64 bytes by its digest, matched identifier-agnostically (minified names change every build) in the 2.1.311 linux-x64 artifact and in the 2.1.308 linux-x64 artifact (sha256 356733f185fa988e6bf3aa9a555269fdd167982a2e2a80d3c8a78037bb92ad58, the promoted bytes), and the code around it compared modulo minified names; each fact below re-read unchanged.

facts.fact: The root command is commander with .argument("[prompt]") and .helpOption("-h, --help"); every root option, listed and hidden (hideHelp), with its arity, is in one builder. Hidden ones rowed by the table: -d2e/--debug-to-stderr, --system-prompt-file, --append-system-prompt-file, --max-turns, --permission-prompt-tool, --remote, --pool, --rc, and now --client-data-url (listed in 2.1.283). Hidden and new since 2.1.283, unrowed (refused as unknown by policy): --fast-mode <on|off> (no parse-time choice check), --allow-other-models, --include-unsupported-models, --host-auth-is-org-sign-in, --proactivity <level> (choices ask, default, proactive, checked at parse), --runner-declares <names>. Listed and new: --desktop.
--desktop is a listed boolean root option: "Open in the Claude Desktop app instead of the terminal (with --continue or --resume <id> to pick the session)".
--proactivity <level> is a root option with commander choices (ask, default, proactive), hidden unless a feature gate lists it.
--runner-declares <names> is a hidden root option taking one value.
--fast-mode <on|off> is a hidden root option; its parser maps anything else to undefined instead of refusing it.
--client-data-url <url> is still a root option taking one value (the parse probe reads mcp help); 2.1.308 no longer lists it in --help.

Before commander: when any argv token is logs|attach|stop|kill|respawn|rm, backgroundSessionVerbIndex(argv, {behindRootOptions: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_KIND !== "bg"}) decides whether it is a background verb (background-verb-index); --bg/--background dispatch only through hasBackgroundFlag (background-flag-value-aware); either path refuses --desktop. remote-control|rc|remote|sync|bridge and self-hosted-runner still dispatch as argv[0] only, daemon after any --dangerously-skip-permissions/--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, and the version fast path is an argv of exactly --version|-v|-V (with --verbose).

A background verb is the first operand (value-aware; after `--` the next token is the operand). At argv[0] it always dispatches. Behind other tokens it dispatches only when behindRootOptions holds (not inside a bg session), the verb does not directly follow `--`, the next token is an 8-hex job id (or respawn --all), and every preceding token is a safe root option (boolean flags such as --verbose, or a value option outside --exec|-m|--handle-uri); -p/--print, --bg, --routine, help, version and short clusters disqualify it. Otherwise the verb is an ordinary operand (a prompt).
--bg/--background count only as option tokens before `--`, skipping option values: `claude -- --bg` and `claude --model --bg` are not background launches (2.1.283 matched the token anywhere).
facts.note: 2.1.311 adds cliFlagWords beside hasBackgroundFlag (the option tokens before `--`, a value-taking option joined to its value) and installs it as the debug logger's argv reader; hasBackgroundFlag itself is unchanged.

facts.fact: --desktop is read by a raw scan of argv before the first `--`, and the background, tmux, print, SDK, init-only, redirected-output, restricted, safe, bare, and restrict-personal-config paths refuse it.

The root command's action launches the Claude Desktop app when commander parsed --desktop (launchDesktopFromCli, with --continue/--resume): commander reads the option, so `-- --desktop` is a prompt and `--model --desktop` takes it as the model's value. The raw scan before `--` (desktop-entry-scan) is used only to refuse it on the background and tmux fast paths.
argv[0] --gh-standin is the entry Claude's own per-session gh shim execs; used directly it exits "gh: this command is run by the gh shim Claude Code writes for a session; it is not for direct use."
(--tmux or --tmux=classic) together with -w/--worktree/--worktree=… anywhere in argv execs into a tmux (or iTerm2) session for the worktree, before commander.
--bare anywhere before the first `--` sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 before commander parses, whatever commander makes of the token; --safe-mode is read the same way (argv before `--`).

Subcommands are registered only when argv has no exact -p/--print option token (value-aware, before `--`) or names a cc:// address; otherwise the program parses with none, and a subcommand name is an operand.
Claude's own pre-parse arity sets (one value, variadic, optional value) used to skip values before commander; 2.1.308 adds the new hidden options to them.
`claude [options] import [codex|gemini|cursor|--dry-run|--yes[=…]]` is rewritten to `claude [options] -- "/import …"` (a session that runs /import) when the feature is on, before commander.

The session permission mode is the first of: --dangerously-skip-permissions (bypassPermissions, unless bypass is disabled), --permission-mode, the agent frontmatter, the settings defaultMode; so --dangerously-skip-permissions wins over any --permission-mode, and a --permission-mode overrides the settings defaultMode.
The eager settings load reads only the last --settings value.
The root program is created with enablePositionalOptions().
The bundled commander's defaults: unknown options refused, excess operands allowed (dropped), combined short flag and optional value on.
attach <id|name>, logs <id|name>, stop|kill, respawn and rm are spliced into the help only; commander does not register them (their dispatch is background-verb-index).
purge [path] is a root subcommand (formerly project purge) with --dry-run, -y/--yes, -i/--interactive and --all; it asks for confirmation unless -y, and tokens after `--` become its [path].
project is registered hidden; its description says `claude project purge` is now `claude purge`, and project purge still runs with a notice.
drop-worktree-registrations is a hidden root subcommand beside the edit-* VS Code helpers, with a required --json flag and its request on stdin ("used by the VS Code extension").

Without print mode the action exits with an error for --prompt-suggestions, --no-session-persistence, --include-partial-messages, --forward-subagent-text, --replay-user-messages and --input-format=stream-json; --json-schema is read only for a non-interactive or background session.
cloudSessionsByDefault and the new sandboxVmByDefault are both hard-coded false at session start.

runtime.method: Credential-less argv shapes whose dispatch changed in 2.1.308, each in a disposable HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/TMPDIR with no TTY, a 15 s bound and the fail-closed model endpoint, on 2.1.311 and on the 2.1.308 linux-x64 artifact (sha256 356733f185fa988e6bf3aa9a555269fdd167982a2e2a80d3c8a78037bb92ad58, the promoted bytes). Only inert shapes run: a job id no job matches, purge in an empty project, the helper without its stdin request, the gh entry used directly. --desktop, --bg, Remote Control and cloud paths stay parse-only.

live.method: The repository's own isolated rig (packages/adapter-claude/src/test-support/live-model.ts): a throwaway HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR per probe (trust and the bypass consent pre-seeded), a loopback Messages API that answers "ok", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN a placeholder, nonessential traffic off, command hooks appending to a throwaway log, the session in a node-pty the harness owns. Nothing of the owner's configuration or account is read or written. <managed hooks> is a settings file whose SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and SessionEnd command hooks log each event.
live.note: The 16 live sessions L01-L16 of the 2.1.283 record were not repeated on 2.1.308 or 2.1.311. Each rests on a static fact above whose anchor was relocated and re-read unchanged, and on parse probes that read identically; their findings carry forward on that evidence only.

adapterClassification.method: How packages/adapter-claude/src/launch/invocation-grammar.ts (CLAUDE_INVOCATION_GRAMMAR_VERSION 2.1.311) classifies each 2.1.308 change; 2.1.311 changes no option, subcommand, arity or dispatch rule, so the rows carry forward. The census test holds the table to help.txt in both directions; the table's option arities equal the CLI's own pre-parse arity sets (pre-parse-arities) row for row.

rows.note: Read wherever commander takes the first operand, `--` included: a managed launch's `-- <prompt>` would hand purge its operands, so an accepted reading's first operand may never name a command subcommand.

argv[0] always; behind tokens only after safe root options, not directly after `--`, and before an 8-hex id (or respawn --all). The reader does not see CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_KIND=bg and reads such a verb as dispatched: a passthrough.

rows.row: entry rule background (the token anywhere, `--` or not)
rows.note: Deliberately broader than 2.1.308: the reader is not version-gated, and 2.1.283 matched the token anywhere, so `-- --bg` and `--model --bg` (a prompt and a model value on 2.1.299+) stay passthroughs rather than managed launches an older release would start in the background.

rows.class: rejected (this adapter does not know it)
rows.note: Unrowed options are refused by policy (findings.md §7); whether any should be carried is open.
